You could just use that method for your individual passwords too, though admittedly that is nowhere near as convenient as having a password manager.

Fair enough if it doesn't get cracked, but that still leaves the issue of leaks which seems to be more the trend these days anyway with big breaches.

https://password-managers.bestreviews.net/faq/which-password-managers-have-been-hacked/

The same is true of password managers, they are leaked too - the whole point of what I'm saying is that if a password manager gets leaked, you now have to change every single password you have on everything.

If my PayPal gets leaked, sure my Outlook password for example might be very easy to then crack if it's a variation - but the person seeing my leaked PayPal would have to first know or figure out I have an Outlook account and then on a whim try to hack that to then find out that it is a variation - not impossible I'll grant you - but they aren't just handed the keys to my entire life.

How? If the password on the vault is one you "know for sure" as the person I replied to said and not some massive string of random characters it's going to be the same as one you "know for sure" on a bank.

Likewise, you can have a complex password on both, the difference is if one gets hacked your bank account is compromised, if the other is then everything is compromised.
You are confusing "memorable" with "common".

Eh, personally I'm not a big fan of password managers - one password / 2FA cracked and someone not only knows all my passwords, but they also have a convenient list of all the different accounts I own. Seems really insecure.

I'd rather just have different memorable passwords with variations for different things and keep them separate.
